stem: A data platform team runs a long-lived Spark cluster with custom-tuned instance types and third-party software installed, processing a sustained, heavy workload around the clock.

choices.text: Query the workload's data ad hoc with Amazon Athena instead
Move the workload to a Glue ETL job with no cluster to manage
Move the workload to Amazon EMR Serverless
Keep the workload on Amazon EMR in cluster mode

rationale: Amazon EMR in cluster mode is built for a long-lived, tunable, multi-node cluster with custom software and fine-grained control over instance types, matching a sustained, heavy, always-on workload with third-party software installed. Athena runs ad hoc SQL over S3 data; it has no concept of a persistent, custom-tuned cluster. A Glue ETL job is serverless and scriptable but does not expose the fine-grained instance-type tuning or ability to install arbitrary third-party software a persistent EMR cluster does. EMR Serverless removes the cluster to manage, which also removes the custom instance-type tuning and installed third-party software the requirement depends on.
